source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 9 (book p. 273); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
Four \(\tan^{-1}\) terms that should add to \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).
Plan: group them as two differences, (1st - 2nd) and (3rd - 4th), and use formula (vi) on each.
steps:
Given: \(\tan^{-1}\frac{10}{3} - \tan^{-1}\frac{7}{13} + \tan^{-1}\frac{9}{5} - \tan^{-1}\frac{2}{7}\).
To prove: it equals \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).
Method: group into two differences and apply formula (vi) \(\tan^{-1}x - \tan^{-1}y = \tan^{-1}\frac{x-y}{1+xy}\) to each. Its condition \(xy > -1\) holds since all numbers are positive.

Add the two pairs
\[\text{L.H.S} = \tfrac{\pi}{4} + \tfrac{\pi}{4} = \tfrac{\pi}{2} = \text{R.H.S}\]
Why: the expression is (first pair) + (second pair), and each pair is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).

Check
\[1.2793 - 0.4939 + 1.0637 - 0.2783\]
\[= 1.5708 \approx \tfrac{\pi}{2}\ \checkmark\]
Why: a calculator in radian mode agrees.
